title: This Is Your Brain, This Is Your Brain During a Pitch
coreMove: Translate dense pitch material into simple, novel, relevant cues that survive the first audience filter.
sourcePressure: Practical brain-model chapter: live audiences first filter for novelty, threat, simplicity, and relevance, so dense analytic material gets blocked before deeper reasoning starts.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must keep the croc brain as a practical filter, not a license for invented neuroscience or crude emotional manipulation.

tryThisNow: Simplify your message in one minute
examples: generic investor deck full of charts

exampleSpecs.domain: airport operations vendor explaining runway-light outage prediction to a control-tower committee
exampleSpecs.audience: a data-heavy product lead facing pilots and maintenance chiefs
exampleSpecs.stakes: the tool is dismissed as another dashboard while night closures keep costing slots
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he replaces the failure-rate table with one blinking runway segment on a live airport map and asks which aircraft gets delayed first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dark runway diagram glowing on a tablet at 5:40 a.m.

exampleSpecs.domain: wildfire insurance analyst briefing a coastal winery group about smoke-taint risk
exampleSpecs.audience: an analyst whose actuarial model is accurate but invisible to growers
exampleSpecs.stakes: growers ignore mitigation until one smoke week wipes out harvest value
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sets the model aside and shows a single vineyard row turning from green to amber on the risk map, then names the harvest week it threatens
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a vineyard risk map spread beside a corkscrew on a tasting counter

exampleSpecs.domain: cybersecurity trainer onboarding harbor pilots to phishing controls
exampleSpecs.audience: a security trainer facing professionals who distrust corporate modules
exampleSpecs.stakes: one stolen credential can halt vessel scheduling for a day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when the pilots tune out the policy language, she projects one fake tide-change email and asks which word would make them click while on watch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a projected email above a chart table with tide books open

exampleSpecs.domain: agricultural drone founder pitching crop-stress imaging to almond growers
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder with spectral data that overwhelms practical buyers
exampleSpecs.stakes: water stress spreads for two weeks before the growers visually notice it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he swaps the spectral graph for two side-by-side orchard rows, one invisible to the eye and one flagged by the drone, then points to the irrigation valve date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two orchard aerial prints clipped to a tailgate

exampleSpecs.domain: rail safety engineer pitching a braking alert to commuter rail supervisors
exampleSpecs.audience: an engineer who keeps opening with equations
exampleSpecs.stakes: supervisors miss why a ten-second warning changes a packed platform morning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes one number on the board, ten seconds, then plays the station audio instead of explaining the full braking model
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a station audio recorder beside a grease-stained timetable

exampleSpecs.domain: specialty pharmacy director explaining cold-chain risk to clinic managers
exampleSpecs.audience: a director who must make handling rules feel immediate without exaggerating danger
exampleSpecs.stakes: one mishandled biologic shipment spoils a week of patient appointments
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she holds up the temperature strip from yesterday's shipment and asks whether the clinic would dose from the box before showing the compliance report
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blue temperature strip sealed in a plastic sleeve

skillTargets: identify first-filter overload in a dense pitch
choose novelty and relevance cues without distorting substance
evaluate when a vivid cue becomes unsupported fear

tryThisNowSpec: Take one dense claim from your pitch and rewrite it as one visible change, one risk, and one reason the listener should care before any detail.
